rationale: salsa20 is a compact ARX stream-cipher kernel whose security and performance live almost entirely in a few extremely hot loops (quarterround/rowround/columnround/doubleround and key expansion), so the table prioritizes transforms whose overhead is per-instruction and semantics-preserving rather than control-flow-inflating: SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because mixing boolean/arithmetic identities is cheap, correct, and directly obscures the add-xor-rotate structure that an analyst keys on, while FLA and BCF are heavily penalized on RuntimeCost and SizeCost since a dispatcher or bogus-edge blowup in the doubleround loop is exactly where runtime overhead becomes unacceptable; SPLIT is favored (low risk, low cost, real diversity on the few multi-block functions) as a low-cost complement, IBR is kept at moderate weight to hide branch structure without paying indirect-branch costs in the hot loop, and ICALL/IGV are down-weighted because this profile shows a call/loop-centric kernel with essentially no large global state or call graph to disguise, so their security payoff here is minimal relative to added indirection cost and correctness risk on pointer-heavy code.
